text: Lunenburg has written itself a report every single year since {ar.first}, and we've now gone through every one of them. 📚

{ar.editions} annual town reports, {ar.first} to {ar.last}: {ar.pages|n} pages in all. Each one is the town's own account of its year: the tax rate, the Assessors' counts, the Treasurer's books, the school rosters, the election results. Every section was written by the people doing the work that year: the Town Clerk, the Assessors, the Treasurer, the school department, every board and committee. The town printed them year after year, for more than six decades, and they are a gift to anyone who wants to know how we got here. Thank you to everyone who wrote their part.
Of those {ar.pages|n} pages, {fin.all.text} hold financial tables. We read every one of them, and {fin.proven.text} check out against totals the town itself printed on the page.
Some things only reading every report can show:

💸 Across all {ar.editions} reports, the highest tax rate printed is {rate.peak.text} {rate.peak.unit}, in {rate.py.text}. Today's, in the FY{ar.last} report, is {rate.last.text}. The two are not comparable: the rate fell by more than a third {rate.n.text} times, each in a year the town revalued ("{reval.quote}"). A rate only compares within one assessment, so neither number tells you what a household paid.
📋 The school rosters printed {rn0.names} names in {rn0.year} and {rnL.names} in {rnL.year}. That counts names, not a staffing level: a roster says nothing about hours or who pays.

🧑‍🏫 The first teacher aide appears on the {fa.a.text} roster: {aide.name}, "{aide.role}". The {fa.b.text} roster prints {fa.n.text} paraprofessionals, the second most common job after classroom teacher.

🏛️ A study committee recommended a town manager in {tm.a.text}, a second committee in {tm2.edition}, and the charter passed in {tm.b.text}, {tm.yes.text} to {tm.no.text}: {tm.n.text} years from first study to charter.
🏡 The fact pages count {pop.a.text} residents in {pop.ay.text} and {pop.b.text} in {pop.by.text}.
👋 Names you might know, from the longest runs on the school rosters:
• {r0.name}: {r0.span} years, {r0.first} to {r0.last}, starting as the boys' phys. ed. instructor.

• {r1.name} ({r1.span} years, from {r1.first}), {r2.name} ({r2.span}, from {r2.first}), {r3.name} ({r3.span}, from {r3.first}), {r4.name} ({r4.span}, from {r4.first}) and {r5.name} ({r5.span}, from {r5.first}).

• {nass.name}: in the school cafeteria from {nass.a.first} to {nass.a.last}, then the same name is back on the rosters in {nass.b.first} under Phys. Ed. One person or two? The reports can't say. Maybe you can!
Did any of them teach you, coach you or serve you lunch? Tag someone who'd remember, and tell us what you remember about Lunenburg in the Sixties, Seventies or Eighties. 👇
